result.note: Tests the May 2026 CCEA approval of SARTHAK-PDS: outlay, timeline and structure, plus its three AI platforms.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about SARTHAK-PDS, approved in May 2026:
items: It was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
It has an outlay of INR 25,530 crore and runs through March 2031.
It merges two existing schemes, pairing financial support for state-level grain transport with a technology layer.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three statements are correct. The CCEA approved the INR 25,530 crore overhaul of the Public Distribution System on 27 May 2026, and it brings two existing schemes under one umbrella. The government expects food grain travel distances to fall by 15–50%, saving roughly INR 280 crore annually.
questions.source: On Wednesday, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved SARTHAK-PDS, an INR 25,530 crore (USD 3 billion) overhaul of the Public Distribution System (PDS) running through March 2031.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs of AI-powered platforms under SARTHAK-PDS, approved in May 2026, and their functions:
items: NIRMAL — Real-time beneficiary registry with cross-ministry integration
ASHA — Route optimisation and QR-code traceability of food grain
SAKSHAM — Vehicle tracking and demand forecasting in grain transport
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: ASHA is wrongly matched: it handles grievance redressal across calls, WhatsApp, IVRS and multilingual chatbots, while route optimisation and QR-code traceability fall under SAKSHAM. SAKSHAM is meant to cut waste in food grain transport.
questions.source: ASHA handles grievance redressal across calls, WhatsApp, IVRS, and multilingual chatbots.
